newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding via system RPs, early move possible.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding via system RPs, early move possible.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add reserves into the banking system via a round of system repurchase agreements Wednesday, analysts said.
The RPs should be two-, five-, or six-days, most agreed to ensure enough reserves through Thanksgiving. The RPs would be a supplement to the 10-day fixed RPs executed Monday.
Tuesday, the Fed added through overnight system RPs, but that doesn't cover the holiday.
With the bond market closing at 1400 EST/1900 GMT, the Fed will likely enter the open market earlier than its usual 1130 EST/1630 GMT intervention period, analysts said.
The Fed is seen entering the market no later than 1030 EST/1530 GMT.
An operation is expected this session because of the pressure on Federal funds. After trading up to seven percent Tuesday, funds opened Wednesday at 5-3/8 percent.

Marc Wanshel, Fed watcher at J.P. Morgan & Co., said that a longer-term operation is most likely, either five-day or six-day system RPs. "The Fed will probably want to take care of most of the add need for the weekend today, rather than attempt to arrange a large operation Friday," he said.
